theme.credits_lede: All photos are from Wikimedia Commons, used under their own licences; authors are listed below. Unless a place is named, most are illustrations from elsewhere in Morocco, not Tangier.

cards.where: Northern tip of Morocco, across the strait from Spain
cards.title: Tangier
sub: What to buy · What to eat
How to haggle · Where to watch the sea
cards.meta: Pre-trip research notes · Prices in dirham (dh), €1 ≈ 10.5 dh

cards.title: One thing first: Tangier doesn't make pottery, it resells it

items.name: What Tangier really produces
items.desc: Only two things: leather, and hand-woven rugs from the Rif mountains

items.name: Everything else is trucked in
items.desc: Pottery from Safi and Fez; brass, woodwork and carpets from Marrakech and Essaouira

items.name: So prices follow a pattern
items.desc: Asking prices run about 2–3× the final price. Counter at one third, settle near 50%

items.name: Where to start
items.desc: Ensemble Artisanal: government-run craft centres with fixed prices. See what the real thing looks like and costs, then go to the open stalls

blocks.text: Haggling pressure is lower than in Marrakech, where guides say the first price is often 4–5× the final one.

items.name: Grand Socco (Place du 9 Avril)
items.desc: Everyday market: fruit, spices, flowers, produce from the Rif

items.name: Around Petit Socco
items.desc: Leather goods, babouche slippers, textiles, cafés

items.name: Rue Siaghine
items.desc: The historic silversmiths' street; now gold, silver and souvenirs

items.name: Rue Mouahidines
items.desc: Densest crafts stalls; watch potters, carpenters and leatherworkers at work

items.name: Near Cinema Rif
items.desc: Up the steps from Grand Socco: the babouche market

items.name: Souk Fondak Chejra
items.desc: Weavers' market; buy hand-woven rugs straight from the weaver

items.name: Around Bab Kasbah
items.desc: Spice stalls

items.name: Babouche slippers
items.desc: Pointed and backless; men's mostly yellow or white, women's embroidered

items.name: Leather jacket
items.desc: The best buy in Tangier; €200+ for the same thing in Europe

blocks.text: Real or fake: soft, springy leather with visible stitching, soles sewn rather than glued. Scratch the back with a fingernail: real leather marks smooth out, PU doesn't.

items.name: Weight
items.desc: Heavy, uneven walls · Factory: uniform thickness

items.name: Painting
items.desc: Visible brushstrokes · Factory: neat and repeating

items.name: Underside
items.desc: Rough and unglazed · Factory: perfectly smooth

items.name: A tap
items.desc: Clear ring · Factory: dull thud

items.name: Same design twice
items.desc: Always differs · Factory: identical

cards.title: The pottery price ladder
cards.lede: Workshop price is the baseline. Medina stalls run 50–100% higher; tourist shops near the sights charge 2–3× the workshop price.

items.name: Small bowl, tea glass
items.desc: Fair medina price

blocks.text: Estimated from workshop prices and typical markups, not measured. Buying a set can save another 15–25%.

items.name: Pierced brass lamp
items.desc: Reach inside the shade: burrs mean handmade, smooth edges mean machine-stamped. Check the weight; brass won't stick to a magnet

items.name: Hand-woven rugs
items.desc: Visit the Fondak Chejra weavers' market, watch them work and buy direct

items.name: Set an anchor
items.desc: Before the souk, check tags on similar goods at a fixed-price co-op. Haggling without an anchor is guessing

items.name: Divide the ask by 2–3
items.desc: A stall's first price is usually 2–3× what it would accept

items.name: Start at one third
items.desc: Aim for about 50%. On small pottery, 40% is realistic

items.name: Bargain for the set
items.desc: Six bowls? Negotiate the total; you can often shave another 15–25%

items.name: Be ready to walk
items.desc: Fix your limit before you go in, and mean it. The price shouted after you is near the real floor

items.name: Don't squeeze to zero
items.desc: They are resellers and craftspeople. Aim for a fair price, not a knockout

blocks.text: Ask the price: bshhal hada? (how much is this?)

items.name: Free guides and “my friend's factory”
items.desc: Whoever walks you to a “cooperative” earns a 20–40% commission, added to your price

items.name: “Antiques”
items.desc: Real antiques are rare in the medina; ageing things is a mature business

items.name: Don't buy on day one
items.desc: Walk a full loop first. Prices often differ on the second day

items.name: Cash is king
items.desc: Carry small dirham notes. The dirham is a closed currency: spend or exchange it before you leave

items.name: Ask before taking photos
items.desc: Many vendors mind, and some raise the price because of it

blocks.text: Pottery is fragile and heavy: confirm the seller packs it in foam and a box, and wrap tagine lid and base separately.

cards.title: Breakfast and street food, a few dirhams each

items.name: Bissara
items.desc: Fava-bean soup with olive oil and cumin. 7–11 am, then sold out

items.name: Sfenj
items.desc: Fried doughnut, not sweet

items.name: Msemen with honey
items.desc: Layered flatbread, breakfast or tea

items.name: Maakouda
items.desc: Fried potato cake, often in bread

items.name: Kalinti
items.desc: Chickpea-flour and egg bake, evenings

cards.title: What to eat for a proper meal

items.name: Harira
items.desc: Tomato, chickpea and lamb soup; evenings

items.name: Brochettes
items.desc: Charcoal-grilled, with bread and hot sauce, per skewer

items.name: Tagine
items.desc: Local places 40–70 dh, tourist areas 80–150 dh

items.name: Couscous
items.desc: Most local places serve it only at Friday lunch

items.name: Grilled fish
items.desc: Sardines, bream, squid with chermoula; best at lunch

items.name: Mint tea
items.desc: Green tea with a fistful of mint and lots of sugar, poured from height. After meals and in the afternoon

items.name: Chebakia
items.desc: Flower-shaped fried pastry in honey and sesame

items.name: Sellou
items.desc: Toasted flour with almonds and sesame, a calorie bomb

items.name: Kaab el ghazal
items.desc: “Gazelle horns”: almond-paste crescents

blocks.text: For proper pastries, go to the pâtisseries in the Ville Nouvelle rather than medina tourist shops. About 10–30 dh a portion.

items.name: Restaurant Bachir
items.desc: Tagine and Friday couscous, very cheap. Packed at lunch: go early

items.name: Chez Hassan
items.desc: Local grill on the way up to the Kasbah: kefta and skewers

items.name: Le Saveur du Poisson
items.desc: No menu, one fixed multi-course seafood meal

items.name: Darna
items.desc: Courtyard under a fig tree, fixed home cooking

items.name: Central fish market
items.desc: Buy fish in the morning, have a nearby stall grill it. Agree the total first

items.name: Café Hafa
items.desc: A clifftop tea terrace since 1921, facing the strait

blocks.text: Per person: street 20–50, local restaurant 50–100, mid-range 120–280, upscale 300–700 dh. Re-check opening status before you go.

items.name: Strangers who offer to lead you
items.desc: Always refuse. Many are unlicensed guides on commission, and some demand big tips afterwards

items.name: No price list
items.desc: A warning sign, not charm. Agree the price before you sit or eat

items.name: Seats facing a landmark
items.desc: Petit Socco, across from Grand Socco, the Kasbah gate: the same tea costs 20–30% more. Walk two alleys in

items.name: Spotting a local place
items.desc: At 12:30–2 pm, see which one is full of local office workers. Friday couscous is a strong signal

items.name: Beach-restaurant drinks
items.desc: Mains may be fair, but a juice at 38 dh is how they make it back

items.name: Plage Municipale
items.desc: City beach in the centre. A 2026 official report lists its water as non-compliant: walk, don't swim

items.name: Malabata / Ghandouri
items.desc: Cleanest water within the city, lifeguards throughout, locals' first choice

items.name: Achakkar
items.desc: 14 km west, 25–30 min by car. Quiet, clear water, main surf spot. Camel ride about 105 dh

blocks.text: To Achakkar: shared grand taxi from Rue Sidi Bouabid, about 20 dh each. Add the Caves of Hercules: 60 dh, best light late afternoon.

cards.title: Four places to watch the sunset

items.name: Café Hafa
items.desc: Clifftop terrace facing the strait. It closes around dusk: arrive before 5 pm for an outer seat

items.name: Cap Spartel / Achakkar
items.desc: Due west on the Atlantic, the widest view, a true sun-into-the-sea sunset. Book your ride back

items.name: Kasbah walls / Marshan viewpoints
items.desc: Free and walkable, with a view of the strait and Spain

items.name: Malabata seafront
items.desc: Faces east: not a sunset spot

cards.title: September: weather and what to wear

items.label: Rain all month, about 4 days; mostly dry
Average wind; an easterly throws sand

items.name: Windy days
items.desc: Head west to Achakkar or find a sheltered bay

items.name: On the beach
items.desc: The city beach is the locals' beach. Conservative swimwear is easiest: a one-piece, or bikini plus T-shirt

items.name: Off the beach
items.desc: Cover up. The seafront promenade counts as street: bring a wrap

items.name: Medina and Kasbah
items.desc: Bare shoulders and knees draw more attention

items.name: Don't buy camphor
items.desc: The most toxic item on the shelf; 1 g can cause seizures in a toddler

items.name: Citrus oil on skin, then sun
items.desc: Pigmentation on neck and collarbone lasts months

items.name: No essential oils by mouth or in the bath
items.desc: They burn skin near-neat: mix with a carrier oil first

items.name: Black soap isn't for faces
items.desc: Potassium soap, pH 9–10. In the eyes: rinse 15 minutes and see a doctor

items.name: Never “black henna”
items.desc: The black comes from PPD: burns, lifelong allergy, scars

items.name: No loose kohl near eyes
items.desc: Often lead-based; over half of tests show dangerous lead levels

cards.title: Saffron: five checks at the stall

blocks.side: Under **25–30 dh/g**, it is almost certainly not pure saffron.

items.name: Whole threads, never powder
items.desc: Powder hides cheaper spices

items.name: Look at the shape
items.desc: Deep red with one orange trumpet end. Uniform red means safflower or corn silk

items.name: Water test
items.desc: Warm water: gold seeps out over 10–15 min, thread stays red. Red water is dye

items.name: Smell
items.desc: Honey-sweet with a hint of metal and hay. Pure perfume-sweet is fake

items.name: Ask for provenance
items.desc: Sealed pack, co-op name, batch number. Co-op price ~40 dh/g

cards.title: Sites worth reading before you go

items.name: Anou
items.desc: Handmade goods to buy. Note the international prices first: your haggling anchor

items.name: Homo Faber Guide · Morocco
items.desc: For arranging workshop visits

items.name: Maison de l'Artisan
items.desc: Official crafts body; look for the Label Artisanat stamp in person

items.name: TasteAtlas · Morocco
items.desc: Use it as a menu dictionary

items.name: MarocMama
items.desc: Recipes and how locals eat

items.name: Visit Morocco (ONMT)
items.desc: National tourist office: promotion and practical procedures

items.name: UNESCO Intangible Heritage list
items.desc: Your baseline for what's authentic

blocks.text: Sites with prices usually sell something.

items.name: Morning
items.desc: Central fish market: buy fish and have a stall grill it. Agree the price first

items.name: Noon
items.desc: Tagine at Restaurant Bachir; go early. On Friday, don't miss the couscous

items.name: Afternoon
items.desc: Shared taxi from beside Grand Socco, 20 dh to Achakkar: swim, camel ride, Caves of Hercules

items.name: Evening
items.desc: Head back, or stay for the sunset. Book the ride home in advance

blocks.text: Food and transport for the day: 200–300 dh (€19–29). Swim only at Malabata or Achakkar; use the city beach for walks.
